native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants varies strongly and systematically by habitat type in the Barcelona province plot network (632 plots): it is highest in low-elevation, human-subsidised and hydric habitats - Wetlands (50.0% of plots, 95% CI 34.8-65.2) and Urban (47.7%, 36.0-59.6), then Coastal (44.8%) and Riparian (36.1%) - intermediate in Croplands (20.7%), and lowest in upland semi-natural habitats, Coniferous forests (6.5%), Broad-leaved forests (4.4%) and Meadows (7.7%), with Scrublands (1.9%) and Rock outcrops (0%) too sparsely colonised to support a rate. The four lowland-disturbed habitats hold 44.0% garden-occupied plots (85/193) versus 6.0% (11/184) in the forest/meadow set - risk difference 38.1 percentage points (30.3-45.9), risk ratio 7.4x, odds ratio 12.4 (6.3-24.2), Fisher p = 9e-19 - and habitat x pathway heterogeneity in plot occupancy is significant beyond chance (chi2 = 139.4, df = 9, Monte-Carlo p <= 0.0001 with 10,000 permutations, seed 20261023; unchanged in direction under the >=20-record restriction, p = 0.002, and under effort rarefaction to 29 plots/habitat, rank rho = 1.00). Because the gardening pathway supplies ~75% of regional introductions in the most recent period (397 of 528 species; 18 -> 54 -> 142 -> 397 across periods) while gardening species occupy fewer habitat types (mean habitat.range 1.95) than unintentional ones (2.77), we hypothesise the habitat gradient is propagule-pressure and disturbance mediated - largely expressed through elevation (occupancy 37.3% in the lowest elevation quartile vs 3.2% in the highest; rho = -0.37) and urban cover within 1 km (rho = +0.38) - but with habitat retaining an independent effect after elevation adjustment (Wetlands/Urban/Coastal/Riparian 8-10x odds vs broad-leaved forest, all p <= 0.004). Prediction: garden-origin species will keep accumulating in urban, wetland, coastal and riparian plots while upland forest, meadow, scrub and rock habitats stay comparatively free of garden introductions.

rank agreement between views quantified (Spearman rho = 0.08). 4) FORMAL TEST: 2 x 10 plot-level Gardening-occupied vs not table, primary p from 10,000-permutation Monte-Carlo chi-square (labels permuted across plots, seed 20261023), asymptotic chi-square reported alongside, plot-level standardised residuals for the gardening column. 5) ROBUSTNESS: restriction to habitats with >=20 occurrence records;
